q: What meets requirement 1?
opts: Enable boot diagnostics on every VM
Install the Azure Monitor Agent and create a data collection rule that sends events and counters to a Log Analytics workspace
Create diagnostic settings on each VM that send to a storage account
Use the Activity log
exp: Guest OS logs and performance counters are collected by the Azure Monitor Agent, configured by data collection rules. The Activity log only records control-plane operations.

q: Complete the plan for requirement 2.
tpl: Create one [[0]] scoped to RG-Prod for all VMs, and attach an [[1]] that sends email and SMS.
exp: A metric alert rule scoped to the resource group (with the VM resource type) monitors every VM in it, including VMs added later. An action group delivers the notifications, such as email or SMS, when the alert fires.

q: What meets requirement 3?
opts: Disable the alert rules every Sunday with a runbook
An alert processing rule that suppresses notifications on a weekly schedule
Remove the SMS receivers from the action group on Sundays
Set the alert severity to 4
exp: An alert processing rule can suppress action group notifications on a recurring schedule, such as every Sunday. Alerts still fire and are recorded, but nobody is paged. Disabling rules with a runbook or editing receivers each week is fragile, and severity doesn't stop notifications.

q: For requirements 4 and 5, answer Yes or No:
stmts: The workspace's interactive retention can be set to 1 year
The Activity log keeps 2 years of events in the portal by default
Sending the Activity log to a Log Analytics workspace (or storage) with a diagnostic setting supports the 2-year requirement
Deleting a VM also deletes its logs from the workspace
exp: Interactive retention can be up to 730 days. The Activity log keeps 90 days unless you export it. Logs stay in the workspace for their retention period after the VM is deleted.

q: What meets requirement 6?
opts: IP flow verify
Connection Monitor, testing from the VMs to api.payments.contoso.com on port 443
Packet capture on every VM
An Activity log alert
exp: Connection Monitor tests connectivity from the VMs to api.payments.contoso.com on port 443 continuously, tracking latency and failures, and can raise alerts. IP flow verify only checks NSG rules for one flow at one moment, packet capture is for deep analysis, and the Activity log records management operations.

q: Where must the vault that backs up the North Europe VMs be?
opts: A Recovery Services vault in North Europe
A Recovery Services vault in West Europe
A Backup vault in any region
A storage account in North Europe
exp: Azure VM backups must go to a Recovery Services vault in the same region as the VMs, so the North Europe VMs need a vault in North Europe. A Backup vault doesn't protect Azure VMs, and a storage account isn't a backup vault.

q: Complete the plan for requirements 2 and 4.
tpl: Protect SQL Server with [[0]], and the on-premises folders with [[1]].
blanks: Azure Backup for SQL Server in Azure VMs
exp: Azure Backup for SQL Server in Azure VMs supports frequent log backups (as often as every 15 minutes) and point-in-time restore. The MARS agent backs up Windows files and folders directly to a Recovery Services vault, without a backup server.

q: What meets requirement 5?
opts: Azure Backup with cross-region restore
Azure Site Recovery replicating the VMs to West Europe, with the vault in West Europe and a recovery plan
Geo-redundant storage for the VM disks
Daily VM snapshots copied to West Europe
exp: Azure Site Recovery continuously replicates the VMs to West Europe and can fail them over within minutes. For Azure-to-Azure DR the vault must be in the target region (West Europe), and a recovery plan controls the failover order. Backup with cross-region restore, GRS disks or snapshots would take far longer to bring the VMs up.

q: What meets requirement 6?
opts: A planned failover every quarter
A test failover into an isolated virtual network
Restoring a backup to a new VM
Stopping replication during the drill
exp: A test failover starts replica VMs in an isolated virtual network, so you can check the DR plan without affecting production or interrupting replication. A planned failover would actually move production, restoring a backup tests backup rather than DR, and stopping replication removes protection.

q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: Cross-region restore needs a GRS vault with cross-region restore enabled
The contracts file share is backed up with a Recovery Services vault
The same North Europe vault should be used for both VM backup and Site Recovery of those VMs
The vault's storage redundancy can be changed after items are protected
exp: CRR needs GRS plus the CRR setting. Azure Files backup uses a Recovery Services vault. The Site Recovery vault belongs in the target region (West Europe), unlike the backup vault. Redundancy is locked once items are protected.

q: Complete the query to show average CPU per computer over the last hour.
tpl:
Perf
| where TimeGenerated > [[0]](1h)
| where CounterName == "% Processor Time"
| [[1]] avg(CounterValue) by Computer
exp: ago(1h) returns the time one hour before now, so the where clause keeps the last hour of data. summarize avg(CounterValue) by Computer then calculates the average CPU for each computer. project only selects columns, and extend adds them.

q: Complete the query to chart events in 15-minute buckets.
tpl:
Event
| summarize count() by bin(TimeGenerated, [[0]])
| [[1]] timechart
exp: KQL time spans are written like 15m (minutes), 1h or 1d, so bin(TimeGenerated, 15m) groups events into 15-minute buckets. render timechart then draws the result as a time chart. plot, chart and draw aren't KQL operators.

q: Complete the statement about alerts.
tpl: Severity [[0]] is the most critical. A fired alert moves from New to [[1]] to Closed.
exp: Alert severity runs from Sev 0 (Critical, the most severe) to Sev 4 (Verbose). Each fired alert also has a user response state — New, Acknowledged or Closed — that you set while handling it.

q: Complete the statement about default retention.
tpl: Platform metrics are kept for about [[0]] days, and the Activity log for [[1]] days.
exp: Platform metrics are kept for 93 days and Activity log events for 90 days. To keep either for longer, or to query them with KQL, send them to a Log Analytics workspace or storage account with a diagnostic setting.

q: Complete the statement about Azure VM backup.
tpl: Backup soft delete keeps deleted backup data for [[0]] days. Instant restore snapshots are kept for [[1]] days by default.
exp: Soft delete keeps deleted backup data for 14 days by default, so it can be recovered after an accident or attack. Instant restore snapshots are kept for 2 days by default (1–5 days with the Standard policy), which makes recent restores much faster.

q: Choose the tool for each question.
tpl:
Why is this flow denied? [[0]]
Where does this traffic go next? [[1]]
exp: IP flow verify checks a specific flow and names the NSG rule that allows or denies it. Next hop shows where Azure routes traffic to an address and which route table is responsible.

q: Complete the statement about Azure-to-Azure disaster recovery.
tpl: Create the Recovery Services vault in the [[0]] region. Crash-consistent recovery points are created every [[1]].
exp: For Azure-to-Azure disaster recovery the vault goes in the target region, so it's still available if the source region fails. Site Recovery creates crash-consistent recovery points every 5 minutes, with app-consistent points at an interval you choose.

q: Complete the command to send a key vault's audit logs to a Log Analytics workspace.
exp: az monitor diagnostic-settings create with --workspace sends the key vault's logs (such as AuditEvent) to a Log Analytics workspace, where you can query them. --storage-account (archive) and --event-hub (streaming) are the other destinations.

q: Complete the statement about Log Analytics retention.
tpl: Default interactive retention is [[0]] days, and the maximum interactive retention is [[1]] days.
exp: Most Log Analytics tables keep data for 30 days of interactive retention by default, and you can set up to 730 days. Long-term retention can keep data for much longer (up to 12 years) at a lower price.

q: Complete the statement about the MARS agent.
tpl: The MARS agent backs up [[0]] up to [[1]] times a day.
blanks: Windows files, folders and system state
exp: The MARS agent backs up Windows files, folders and system state directly to a Recovery Services vault, up to three times a day. It doesn't back up whole Hyper-V hosts (MABS or DPM does that), Linux file systems or Azure SQL databases.

q: Match each question to the data source that answers it.
items: Who read or wrote blobs in a storage account?
What do the Windows event logs on the VMs show?
What was a VM's CPU trend over 24 hours?
targets: Azure Monitor Agent + DCR to Log Analytics
Storage resource logs via diagnostic settings
exp: Storage resource logs, sent with a diagnostic setting, record data-plane operations such as who read or wrote blobs. The Activity log records control-plane operations such as deleting a resource. Windows event logs need the Azure Monitor Agent with a DCR sending to Log Analytics. CPU trends come from platform metrics, which are collected automatically.

q: Match each condition to the alert type.
items: An Azure outage in your region
exp: Log search alerts run KQL; Service Health alerts cover Azure incidents; metric alerts watch numbers like CPU; Activity log alerts watch operations such as deletions.

q: Match each workload to the vault type that protects it.
items: SQL Server in an Azure VM
exp: Recovery Services vaults protect Azure VMs, Azure file shares and SQL Server in Azure VMs. Backup vaults protect newer workloads such as Azure Blobs, managed disks and Azure Database for PostgreSQL.

q: Match each scenario to the restore option.
items: Restore a VM in the paired region
Roll back the disks of the same VM
Rebuild a VM with a different size
exp: Cross-region restore uses the secondary region; file recovery mounts a recovery point; Replace existing swaps disks; restoring disks with a template allows changes.

q: Match each goal to the failover recovery point option.
exp: Latest processes all pending data first, giving the lowest data loss (RPO) but a slower failover. Latest processed uses the newest point that's already processed, giving the fastest failover (RTO). Latest app-consistent uses the last application-consistent point, so apps start in a consistent state.

q: Match each need to the Azure Monitor feature.
items: Define what the Azure Monitor Agent collects
Build an interactive report with queries and charts
Send email and SMS and run a runbook
exp: A data collection rule defines what the Azure Monitor Agent collects and where it sends it. A workbook is an interactive report with queries and charts. An alert processing rule can silence notifications during maintenance. An action group sends email and SMS and can run a runbook.

q: Match each task to the KQL operator.
exp: extend adds a calculated column, where filters rows, project picks which columns to show, and summarize aggregates rows (counts, averages and so on, optionally by group). render draws charts.

q: Match each description to the backup component.
items: Coordinates snapshots for Azure VM backup
Backs up on-premises Windows files directly to Azure
App-aware backup of on-premises SQL Server and Hyper-V
exp: The VM backup extension coordinates snapshots for Azure VM backup. The MARS agent backs up on-premises Windows files and folders directly to Azure. MABS and DPM provide app-aware backup of on-premises workloads such as SQL Server and Hyper-V.

code:
Event
| where EventLevelName == "Error"
| summarize Errors = count() by Computer
| top 5 by Errors desc
q: What does this query return?
opts: The five computers with the most error events
The first five error events
Computers with exactly five errors
Error counts for every computer, sorted A–Z
exp: The query keeps only error events, counts them for each computer (summarize count() by Computer), then keeps the five computers with the highest counts (top 5 by Errors desc). It doesn't return the first five events, filter for exactly five, or sort alphabetically.

q: Review the metric alert rule. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: It covers VMs created later in RG-Prod
It is evaluated every minute over a 10-minute window
It resolves automatically when CPU drops
It fires when a single sample is above 85%, even if the 10-minute average is lower
exp: Scoping to a resource group with a target resource type covers new VMs. windowSize and evaluationFrequency set the window and frequency. autoMitigate resolves the alert. The condition uses the average, not individual samples.

code:
AzureActivity
| where OperationNameValue endswith "DELETE"
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, ResourceGroup, _ResourceId
q: What does this query return, and what must be set up first?
opts: Resources deleted in the last 7 days and who deleted them; the Activity log must be sent to the workspace
Failed deployments; nothing needs setting up
Deleted blobs; the storage account needs diagnostic settings
Deleted users; Entra ID P2 is needed
exp: AzureActivity holds control-plane operations once a diagnostic setting sends the Activity log to the workspace. The query filters delete operations from the last 7 days.

code:
$ az backup job list -g RG1 -v rsv1 -o table
Operation  Status      Item Name  Start Time UTC        Duration
---------  ----------  ---------  --------------------  --------
Backup     Completed   vm-web1    2026-11-15T22:00:05   0:12:44
Backup     Failed      vm-sql1    2026-11-15T22:00:07   0:00:31
Restore    InProgress  vm-app2    2026-11-16T08:12:10   0:05:02
q: Review the backup jobs. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: vm-sql1 has a new recovery point from last night
A restore is running now
vm-web1's backup took about 13 minutes
Failed backup jobs can raise built-in Azure Monitor alerts
exp: vm-sql1's backup failed, so it has no new recovery point. The Restore job is in progress. 0:12:44 is about 13 minutes. Azure Backup has built-in Azure Monitor alerts for job failures.

q: Which statement describes this backup policy?
opts: Backups run daily at 23:00 UTC; daily points are kept 30 days and monthly points 12 months; snapshots stay local for 2 days
Backups run every 2 days and are kept 30 days
Backups run hourly and are kept 12 months
Only monthly backups are kept
exp: The schedule runs daily at 23:00 UTC. The retention policy keeps 30 daily and 12 monthly points, and instantRpRetentionRangeInDays keeps snapshots locally for 2 days.

code:
Name     Replication health  Status     RPO
vm-web1  Healthy             Protected  2 min
vm-sql1  Critical            Protected  3 h 10 min
q: What does this replication status mean for vm-sql1?
opts: It is fully protected with no data at risk
A failover now could lose about 3 hours of data, so replication needs investigating
It has already failed over
Its backups have failed
exp: RPO shows how far behind the replica is. An RPO of about 3 hours with Critical health means recent changes haven't reached the target region, so a failover now could lose about 3 hours of data. Investigate replication — for example network or disk churn issues. It hasn't failed over, and this has nothing to do with backups.

code:
Test group:   tg-payment
Source:       vm-app1
Destination:  api.payments.contoso.com:443
Checks failed (%):     0.0
Round-trip time (ms):  avg 38, max 210
q: Review the Connection Monitor results. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: Connectivity to the payment API is currently healthy
An alert can fire when round-trip time passes a threshold
The results are stored in Log Analytics
Connection Monitor captures full packet contents
exp: 0% failed checks means connectivity is healthy. Connection Monitor exposes metrics for alerting and stores data in Log Analytics. It does not capture packets; packet capture does.

q: What does this data collection rule collect?
opts: All Windows events and all performance counters
Only successful and failed logon security events, plus CPU and available memory every 60 seconds, sent to law-prod
Only Linux syslog
Activity log events
exp: The XPath query keeps only Security event IDs 4624 (successful logon) and 4625 (failed logon). Two performance counters, CPU and available memory, are sampled every 60 seconds, and everything goes to the law-prod workspace. It doesn't collect all events, Linux syslog or Activity log events.

q: What does this Activity log event show?
opts: ali@contoso.com successfully deleted the VM vm-old
vm-old crashed
ali@contoso.com tried to delete vm-old, but a lock stopped it
vm-old was moved to another resource group
exp: The operation is Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/delete, the caller is ali@contoso.com and the status is Succeeded, so Ali successfully deleted vm-old. A lock would have produced a Failed status, and a move or crash would show different operations.

code:
Scope:      /subscriptions/1111/resourceGroups/RG-Prod
Rule type:  Suppress notifications
Schedule:   Weekly, Sunday 01:00–03:00 (UTC+05:00)
q: Review the alert processing rule. Answer Yes or No:
stmts: Alerts still fire and show in Azure Monitor during the window
Action groups do not send email during the window
The rule affects alerts for resources in other resource groups
The alert rules are disabled during the window
exp: An alert processing rule with suppression only stops action groups, so alerts still fire and appear in Azure Monitor but no email is sent during the window. Its scope is RG-Prod, so it doesn't affect other resource groups. The alert rules themselves stay enabled.

code:
Next hop type:  VirtualAppliance
IP address:     10.0.1.4
Route table ID: /subscriptions/1111/resourceGroups/RG-Net/providers/Microsoft.Network/routeTables/rt-spoke-app
q: What does this next hop result tell you?
opts: The traffic goes straight to the internet
A user-defined route in rt-spoke-app sends the traffic to the network virtual appliance at 10.0.1.4
An NSG blocks the traffic
The traffic uses VNet peering only
exp: The next hop type is VirtualAppliance with IP 10.0.1.4, and the result names the route table rt-spoke-app. So a user-defined route in that table sends the traffic to the network virtual appliance. It isn't going straight to the internet or using peering only, and next hop doesn't evaluate NSGs.

code:
AddonAzureBackupJobs
| where JobOperation == "Backup" and JobStatus == "Failed"
| summarize Failures = count() by BackupItemUniqueId
q: This query returns no rows even though backups have failed. What is the most likely reason?
opts: Backup jobs are never logged
The vault has no diagnostic setting sending Azure Backup data (resource-specific tables) to this workspace
The query needs Entra ID P2
Failed jobs are deleted after 1 hour
exp: The AddonAzureBackup* tables are only filled when the vault has a diagnostic setting sending Azure Backup data, in resource-specific mode, to that workspace. Without it, the query finds nothing even though jobs failed. Backup jobs are logged, no Entra licence is needed, and failed jobs aren't deleted after an hour.
